verdicts.summary: The adapter's lifecycle hazards are the ones findings 0 and 1 already raise: a bare status:null frame marks a compaction stopped, and a later boundary reuses the stale completed item. I tried other cases: a repeated 'compacting' frame, a status:null frame carrying permissionMode, and frames falling through to later handlers. None adds a new failure. No status handler comes after 7270, so the early returns at 7181 and 7218 skip nothing. permissionMode is applied before dispatch at 8687-8693.

Web and mobile cannot stay stuck in isCompacting after the run ends. The adapter emits a failed or interrupted update for a running compaction item at every turn finalization. On top of that, web gates on phase and mobile gates on an active runtime.
verdicts.scenario: An automatic compaction is running (status 'compacting' frame), and then the user interrupts, the query exits, or a result arrives before any compact_result or boundary frame. finalizeActiveTurn emits the same item id as interrupted or failed. compactionRunning in ChatView.tsx:2526-2532 becomes false, and compactionSettled covers the /compact fallback. Even if no update were emitted, ChatView.tsx:2534 requires phase running/connecting or isSendBusy, and mobile requires threadRuntimeIsActive.
